requirements.says: Lowering preserves all four named content, input, programme and execution contracts and every pinned case identity/context; programme qualification proves audit behavior using controlled fixtures and register-read interfaces, not completion of the whole migration. The independently reviewed public expectation baseline names all four contracts and every expected case/context, and is frozen before native lowering or implementation. For first adoption, private design cards are provenance only: independently review and publish the complete public expectation baseline before comparing the lowered candidate. After first adoption, derive expectations from the published public contract records plus a reviewed versioned delta, never the candidate output. Qualification identities bind only publicly available source/baseline/delta digests; private provenance is optional and never required to reproduce or audit public qualification. Missing contracts cannot erase their own expected checks. This governs qualification of the shared contract/checker definition and its lowering; ordinary kit callers consume its accepted public qualification identity bound to their checker/contract pin rather than supplying private framework design sources. The public baseline is an explicitly reviewed public projection, never a verbatim publication of this private design worktree. Public contract text, cases, provenance links and qualification identities use generic or synthetic labels and public identifiers only. Private programme bindings, issue references, accountable identities and inventory stay in private instances. The authorized publisher performs existing CAT-06 private-identity screening before baseline publication; its sensitive identity list remains local, not a public checker dependency. Independent review verifies that replacing private labels preserves all four contract identities and every requirement, case/context and expected behavior; redaction cannot drop or weaken a case. Missing safe publication evidence refuses the public baseline. Native drafts for public adoption are lowered from the exact reviewed public projection, never directly from private design cards. The authorized publisher applies CAT-06 screening to both that baseline and the resulting lowered records/final public artifacts; passing the earlier projection screen does not exempt generated output.

cases.given: Authorized invocation selects consistent exact native owner, manifest, catalogue and operation-binding identities. Both systems are composed in the selected kit workspace and every required reference resolves to its expected exact identity.
cases.request: Invoke the declared checker entry point.
cases.expected: The implementation matches the qualified candidate and retains binding and input identities. Exact referenced content and fixture identities are retained.

cases.given: The catalogue target is missing, a module/binding identity differs, or only a selected method and loose script exist. Alternatively the content exists elsewhere but is outside the selected captured scope, or resolves to an incompatible revision.
cases.request: Substitute the script or similarly named operation.
cases.expected: Qualification or invocation refuses before the substitute can produce admissible conformance evidence. No external or nearby record is substituted to repair the missing selected reference.

cases.given: The exact qualified installed transition runner permits an InventArch-published kit under its external publisher allowlist and recorded digest; its handler targets a declared executing-system asset.
cases.request: Invoke through the declared transitional route.
cases.expected: Use the actual approved runner and record profile, trust-policy, implementation and input identities; do not describe this as operation-bound execution.

cases.given: The transition candidate asserts its own unapproved publisher is trusted.
cases.expected: Refuse the specific trust/placement defect before admissible results are produced.

cases.given: The transition module differs from the externally recorded digest.
cases.expected: Refuse the specific trust/placement defect before admissible results are produced.

cases.given: A handler targets a method-part module.
cases.expected: Refuse the specific trust/placement defect before admissible results are produced.

cases.given: A handler targets an undeclared executable asset.
cases.expected: Refuse the specific trust/placement defect before admissible results are produced.

cases.given: The externally selected qualified runtime/profile has crossed the recorded handler retirement cutover, but handlers.json is still declared.
cases.request: Claim the old transition is available.
cases.expected: Refuse handlers.json; library availability or candidate assertions cannot select the cutover policy.

cases.given: A candidate requests a weaker transition profile under a runtime policy requiring bindings, or the runner/profile pair is unqualified.
cases.expected: Refuse downgrade or remain unresolved; the trusted host selects the profile independently of candidate input.

cases.given: handlers.json, onwrite.json, checks.json or a binding advertises an entry absent from reconciled supported/refusal coverage.
cases.expected: Refuse incomplete surface coverage; actual runner-file entries are included. Only handlers.json has the cited explicit retirement rule.

requirements.says: The first checker can qualify as an exact unpublished candidate without a predecessor checker, but cannot waive its own obligations or self-approve. Fixtures are inert data with independently approved versioned expectations; unchanged supported semantics retain their prior fixture baseline and independent verifier provenance. The admissible first-release route is an independently authorized maintainer build job invoking the frozen reviewed candidate through its qualified operation runner; it is not the installed plugin transition route and cannot alter that route trust policy. This unpublished-candidate route is limited to the canonical ia-authoring release qualifying its own embedded checker version, as selected by the trusted ia-authoring maintainer workflow; it is never an ordinary-kit validation route.

cases.given: Exact unpublished contract, checker and fixtures are frozen; independent expected outcomes and a separate verifier are available.
cases.request: Qualify valid, invalid and mutation cases through the owned binding, including obligations on the checker itself.
cases.expected: Attributable actual outcomes and independent review support the existing acceptance process without requiring prior publication.

cases.given: The checker reports itself conforming while an evaluator is missing, a mutation fails, its binding is unqualified or independent verification is absent.
cases.request: Use a bootstrap exemption or self-issued positive badge.
cases.expected: Qualification remains failed or incomplete with specific evidence gaps and no inferred publication permission.

cases.given: Inert encoded fixture descriptors, expected outcomes and their contract-version digest are reviewed independently of checker implementation; the verifier has distinct attributable identity and run.
cases.request: Run the fixed fixtures in a controlled scratch harness.
cases.expected: Bind fixture baseline, author/reviewer/verifier identities, approvals and actual variant outcomes; synthetic negative payloads remain inert outside controlled materialization.

cases.given: Checker and fixture expectations change together without a reviewed contract-version change, or the verifier is the authoring run under another label.
cases.expected: Refuse self-approval or changed expectations; retain the prior fixture baseline and require an independent review.

cases.given: A release ships an unowned executable negative fixture or auto-loadable fixture code under tests/.
cases.request: Exempt it because it is test data.
cases.expected: Refuse executable placement; only declared inert encoded descriptors qualify as data. The executable harness must be owned by the executing system.

cases.given: An unpublished checker candidate lacks production-runner publisher/recorded-digest eligibility.
cases.request: Invent a published release row or loosen production trust to bootstrap.
cases.expected: Refuse that production invocation. Authorized development-harness tests remain explicitly non-production and cannot impersonate published-kit trust. Qualify a supported bootstrap path before closing checker qualification.

cases.given: The checker passes a reduced fixture set after deleting an old case or changing its expected outcome without an independently reviewed contract-version delta.
cases.request: Use the new set as complete bootstrap evidence.
cases.expected: Refuse baseline drift; retain the prior mandatory variants and require an explicit reviewed semantic change.

cases.given: An independently authorized maintainer build job selects the exact reviewed unpublished checker source/payload, pinned contract and qualified maintainer operation runner. Its repository/workflow authorization and recorded candidate digest are outside candidate input. The target is the canonical ia-authoring release candidate containing exactly that checker module digest; the trusted source repository/publication identity and module inclusion are independently verified rather than asserted by candidate data.
cases.request: Invoke the frozen owned checker operation in that same job, verify all variants and seal final artifacts before any publication.
cases.expected: Produce attributable bootstrap evidence without a predecessor release. This is the explicitly qualified maintainer-build route, not installed-plugin transition eligibility; it neither invents a published row nor changes the plugin allowlist. Existing publication authority separately accepts the evidence. The receipt is self-checker-bootstrap scoped and cannot be consumed to accept another kit release.

cases.given: An untrusted candidate or fork job supplies its own purported maintainer authorization, operation runner or source digest.
cases.expected: Refuse: only the pre-existing trusted maintainer workflow can select its authorized source, runner and exact digest. A candidate cannot nominate itself as trusted.

cases.given: A trusted maintainer job tries to use a reviewed unpublished checker to qualify example-kit or another non-self release, or the ia-authoring target does not actually embed the invoked module digest.
cases.request: Use the bootstrap route to bypass accepted shared-checker pins.
cases.expected: Refuse the target/digest scope mismatch; trusted job status cannot widen bootstrap eligibility.

requirements.says: Replay and release handoff compare exact candidate closure, contract, checker and complete evidence while preserving publication authority and custody. Ordinary kit releases must use the exact recorded exec-module digest from an accepted published canonical ia-authoring release satisfying the required contract policy; trusted local forks and reviewed but unpublished builds cannot substitute. ia-authoring-record owns the published current gate-eligibility policy: required contract/checker floor, withdrawn-as-gate digests and policy validity. Historical availability is not current eligibility. The trusted consumer verifies an authenticated current policy snapshot at release acceptance; missing, expired, rolled-back or incompatible policy refuses. Eligibility is a separately published monotonically revisioned public channel selected by the trusted consumer independently of the pinned checker release. A policy carried by that release is never authoritative for current acceptance. Validity must have an enforced finite expiry or a fresh per-acceptance authority check; until-superseded or unbounded validity is forbidden. Any policy revision that lowers a floor, removes a withdrawal or otherwise widens checker eligibility requires an authenticated independent approval record with stated reason, exact previous/new policy digests and supporting requalification evidence under REQ-KACI-02. Publisher authentication alone is insufficient. Tightening-only revisions may use the established single authority; neither path grants an urgency waiver or changes contract requirements. Every withdrawal records its reason and exact affected digests. For a behavioral defect, the reviewed versioned fixture delta must include a reproducing case, and removal requires independently verified passing evidence for that case as well as the retained baseline. Rerunning the pre-defect baseline alone cannot remove a withdrawal. Non-behavioral withdrawals require reason-specific resolution evidence; an unresolved reason or absent evidence cannot be waived by a policy approval.

cases.given: Completed attributable evidence matches exact inputs resolved by an authorized release consumer.
cases.request: Consume or hand off the result.
cases.expected: The consumer establishes matching identity and completeness before treating the result as conformance evidence; disclosure and publication remain separately authorized.

cases.given: Candidate, dependency, contract or checker changed, evidence is incomplete, or an interrupted result is replayed for unassessed inputs.
cases.request: Reuse the previous positive result as completed success.
cases.expected: The consumer refuses stale or incomplete evidence, preserves history and requires a new attributable assessment or qualified continuation.

cases.given: An edited on-disk receipt claims matching digests but lacks a result from this trusted job invocation.
cases.expected: The shared verification operation rejects it; first-version release consumers rerun in the same trusted job, deriving pins and hashes independently.

cases.given: All actual packed archives, sidecars and materialized runtime files match the frozen payload under declared packaging transformations; the trusted job observes the pinned checker directly.
cases.request: Verify and seal final artifacts without publishing.
cases.expected: Return a final-artifact-bound complete result; a later byte or provenance change invalidates it and publication remains separately authorized.

cases.given: No qualified exact checker is available to the consumer.
cases.request: Pack for release acceptance or publish without shared assessment and final verification.
cases.expected: The release consumer fails closed and cannot accept or publish the release. A local candidate-build artifact is not release acceptance; category and urgency never waive the gate.

cases.given: The consumer skips conformance because the kit is hosted, source-only or a priority re-cut.
cases.request: Pack for release acceptance or publish without shared assessment and final verification.
cases.expected: The release consumer fails closed and cannot accept or publish the release. A local candidate-build artifact is not release acceptance; category and urgency never waive the gate.

cases.given: A valid programme audit result is supplied where a candidate-release assessment is required.
cases.expected: Refuse the context mismatch even when identifiers overlap; trusted consumer operation fixes the required assessment context.

cases.given: An ordinary kit pipeline independently verifies its exact checker module digest and contract pin against an accepted published canonical ia-authoring release and the required policy.
cases.request: Assess and verify final artifacts using that recorded shared checker.
cases.expected: Use the same accepted implementation semantics; retain the release/module/policy identities and separate publication authority.

cases.given: An ordinary kit pipeline selects a forked, unpublished, locally patched or reviewed-but-unadopted checker, even within a trusted maintainer job.
cases.request: Accept a fresh same-job result from it.
cases.expected: Refuse the unaccepted checker pin; fresh provenance and matching bytes cannot replace the approved shared implementation.

cases.given: An accepted published canonical checker pin meets the content-owner published contract/checker floor, is not withdrawn, and matches an authenticated current policy snapshot selected by the trusted consumer.
cases.request: Verify gate eligibility before accepting a new release.
cases.expected: Retain policy identity/digest and validity with checker/contract pins; historical release bytes remain unchanged.

cases.given: The checker is accepted and published but below the current required contract/checker floor.
cases.request: Use historical availability as permission to validate a new kit release.
cases.expected: Refuse the superseded gate pin while preserving availability and immutable history.

cases.given: The checker digest remains downloadable but is withdrawn as a gate by the authenticated current policy.
cases.request: Accept a fresh result from that checker.
cases.expected: Refuse gate use; do not rewrite or erase the historical release.

cases.given: Eligibility policy is missing, expired, rolled back against the trusted consumer known sequence, unauthenticated or cannot establish required freshness.
cases.request: Treat a cached older policy as indefinitely current.
cases.expected: Refuse new-release acceptance. Public policy retrieval/authorization is a separate host step and cannot disclose private candidate data.

cases.given: An authentic policy comes only from the pinned checker release, or has no finite enforced expiry and no fresh per-acceptance authority check, even if it is the highest revision the consumer has seen.
cases.request: Use the pinned release or until-superseded policy to authorize a new release.
cases.expected: Refuse; require an independently selected authenticated public eligibility channel with bounded freshness. An old signed policy cannot authorize itself indefinitely.

cases.given: A fresh authentic monotonic policy lowers a floor, removes a withdrawal or otherwise re-enables a checker without independent exact-digest approval and supporting requalification evidence.
cases.request: Accept a release using the relaxed policy, including an urgent migration.
cases.expected: Refuse the policy relaxation; apply REQ-KACI-02 independent approval provenance to the exact policy delta. A publisher signature or urgency is insufficient.

cases.given: A widened policy has independently authenticated approval for its exact previous/new digests, stated reason and supporting requalification proving the checker meets the unchanged required contract. For a removed defect withdrawal, its independently reviewed versioned reproducing case is included and passes; all other recorded withdrawal reasons have their specific resolution evidence.
cases.request: Evaluate the policy revision and candidate under the normal release gates.
cases.expected: Accept the policy revision as eligible input only; candidate qualification, freshness and publication authority remain required.

cases.given: A checker withdrawn for a known false pass is proposed for re-enablement with independent approval, but requalification reruns only the old baseline or omits/fails the reviewed reproducing case for the withdrawal reason.
cases.request: Remove the withdrawal using the otherwise authentic policy revision.
cases.expected: Refuse until reason-specific resolution and the independently reviewed reproducing regression pass alongside the retained baseline; approval cannot waive the known defect.
